_comment: Bundle 1 (G items 4 + 5) E2E — round-trip docx through Google Docs. Workflow: agent creates a Google Doc, populates content via append_markdown, exports the doc as docx (G item 5 — attachment plumbing produces a document_id), then re-creates a Google Doc from that docx attachment (G item 4 — attachment fetch). The final report confirms both doc URLs + the docx attachment_id. Requires OAuth env (COLMENA_GOOGLE_OAUTH_*) + GEMINI_API_KEY + DATABASE_URL. Run: `set -a; source .env; set +a; cargo run --bin dag_engine -- run tests/graphs/agents/gdocs_bundle1_e2e.json --agent-session-id g_bundle1_$(date +%s) --include-extra-info`

test_payload.prompt:
You are exercising the Bundle 1 attachment plumbing for Google Docs. Execute this EXACT sequence and report what each tool returned (no inventing).

1. gdocs_create({title: 'Bundle1 E2E Source <UTC iso>'}). Capture doc_id and url.
2. gdocs_append_markdown({doc_id: <step1.doc_id>, markdown: '# Bundle 1 E2E

This document was created by the bundle1 test. It contains a paragraph and a list.

## Items

- alpha
- beta
- gamma
'}).
3. gdocs_export({doc_id: <step1.doc_id>, format: 'docx'}). This calls the G item 5 wrap — the result MUST include a document_id (the exported docx as a new attachment) plus filename + byte_len. Capture document_id_docx.
4. gdocs_create_from_docx({title: 'Bundle1 E2E Roundtrip <UTC iso>', attachment_id: <step3.document_id_docx>}). This is the G item 4 fetch — the server reads the docx bytes from the catalog. Capture new doc_id_roundtrip + url_roundtrip.
5. gdocs_read_as_markdown({doc_id: <step4.doc_id_roundtrip>}). Verify the H1 'Bundle 1 E2E' and the list items appear.

Final report (<200 words): one line per step with the actual values returned, then both doc URLs and the docx attachment_id.

config.system_message: You are a strict testing agent for the colmena Bundle 1 plumbing. Use ONLY the gdocs_* tool names. Do not invent inputs. If a tool returns an error, report it verbatim and stop.
